This Annual Report on Form 10-K (“Form 10-K”) contains forward-looking statements, within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, that involve risks and uncertainties. Forward-looking statements can be identified by words such as “anticipate,” “believe,” “expect,” “may,” “plan,” “will” and similar terms. Forward-looking statements are not guarantees of future performance and the Company’s actual results may differ significantly from the results discussed in the forward-looking statements. All information presented herein is based on the Company’s fiscal calendar, and references to particular years, quarters, months or periods refer to the Company’s fiscal years ended in September and the associated quarters, months and periods of those fiscal years. Unless otherwise stated, references to “we,” “our,” “the Company” and “Fixture Fruit” refer to Fixture Fruit Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.

PART I

Item 1.    Business

Company Background

The Company designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services. The Company’s fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. Fiscal 2024 spanned 52 weeks and ended on September 28, 2024; fiscal 2023 spanned 53 weeks and ended on September 30, 2023.

Products

Orchard Phone. The Company’s line of smartphones based on its Orchard operating system. Orchard Phone accounted for approximately 51% of total net sales in fiscal 2024.

Orchard Book. The Company’s line of personal computers, including notebooks and desktops.

Orchard Pad. The Company’s line of multipurpose tablets.

Wearables, Home and Accessories. Smartwatches, wireless headphones, smart speakers and third-party accessories. In the first quarter of fiscal 2024 the Company sold its Grove accessories business, a distributor of third-party cases and chargers, to a private buyer.

Services

The Company’s services include advertising, cloud storage, digital content subscriptions, payment services and extended warranty programs. Services revenue is recognized over the subscription term and carries a substantially higher gross margin than products.

Markets and Distribution

The Company sells through its retail and online stores, its direct sales force, and third-party cellular network carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers. Sales through indirect distribution channels accounted for approximately 62% of total net sales in fiscal 2024. The Company’s customers are primarily in the consumer, small and mid-sized business, education, enterprise and government markets.

Competition

The markets for the Company’s products and services are highly competitive and are characterized by aggressive price competition, frequent product introductions, short product life cycles, evolving industry standards and rapid adoption of technological advancements. Many of the Company’s competitors sell their products at lower prices and have broader product lines. The Company’s ability to compete successfully depends heavily on ensuring the continuing and timely introduction of innovative products, services and technologies.

Supply of Components

Substantially all of the Company’s hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners located primarily in Asia. Certain components, including advanced display panels and application processors, are currently obtained from single or limited sources. The Company has entered into agreements for the supply of many components; however, there can be no guarantee that the Company will be able to extend or renew these agreements on similar terms.

Human Capital

As of September 28, 2024, the Company had approximately 163,000 full-time equivalent employees. Following the restructuring of its European distribution operations described in Part II, Item 7 of this Form 10-K, headcount in the Europe segment declined by approximately 1,900 during fiscal 2024.

Available Information

The Company’s Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Current Reports on Form 8-K are filed with the SEC and are available free of charge on the Company’s investor relations website.

Item 1A.  Risk Factors

The Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including those described below. When any one or more of these risks materialize from time to time, the Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price can be materially and adversely affected. Because of the following factors, as well as other factors affecting the Company’s results of operations and financial condition, past financial performance should not be considered to be a reliable indicator of future performance, and investors should not use historical trends to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

Macroeconomic and Industry Risks

The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions and adverse economic conditions can materially adversely affect the Company’s business, results of operations and financial condition.

Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth or recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates, and currency fluctuations, can adversely impact consumer confidence and spending and materially adversely affect demand for the Company’s products and services. In addition, consumer confidence and spending can be materially adversely affected in response to changes in fiscal and monetary policy, financial market volatility, declines in income or asset values, and other economic factors. A strong U.S. dollar reduced the Company’s reported net sales in Europe and Greater China by approximately $4.2 billion in fiscal 2024 compared to constant-currency growth.

The Company’s business can be impacted by political events, trade and other international disputes, war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health issues, industrial accidents and other business interruptions.

Political events, trade and other international disputes, war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health issues, industrial accidents and other business interruptions can harm or disrupt international commerce and the global economy, and could have a material adverse effect on the Company and its customers, suppliers, contract manufacturers, distributors and other partners. Substantially all of the Company’s manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in Asia, including China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. Tariffs on products imported into the United States from China mainland, or retaliatory measures, could increase the cost of the Company’s products or reduce demand for them.

Global markets for the Company’s products and services are highly competitive and subject to rapid technological change, and the Company may be unable to compete effectively in these markets.

The Company’s products and services compete in highly competitive global markets characterized by aggressive price competition and resulting downward pressure on gross margins, frequent introduction of new products and services, short product life cycles, evolving industry standards, continual improvement in product price and performance characteristics, rapid adoption of technological advancements by competitors, and price sensitivity on the part of consumers and businesses. The Company’s competitors that sell smartphones and personal computers based on other operating systems have aggressively cut prices and lowered their product margins to gain or maintain market share.

Business Risks

The Company depends on component and product manufacturing and logistical services provided by outsourcing partners, many of which are located outside of the U.S.

Substantially all of the Company’s manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners, and a significant concentration of this manufacturing is currently performed by a small number of outsourcing partners, often in single locations. The Company has also outsourced much of its transportation and logistics management. Although arrangements with these partners may contain provisions for product defect expense reimbursement, the Company generally remains responsible to the consumer for warranty and out-of-warranty service.

The Company’s services business is subject to risks that could reduce its growth rate and gross margin.

The Company’s services revenue depends on continued growth in its installed base, on renewals of digital content subscriptions and on the licensing arrangement under which a third-party search engine is the default on the Company’s devices. Regulatory or judicial changes affecting that arrangement could materially reduce services revenue and gross margin, which, as discussed in Item 7 of this report, has been the primary driver of the Company’s margin expansion since fiscal 2022.

The Company is subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide, which exposes the Company to potential liabilities, increased costs and other adverse effects on the Company’s business.

The Company’s global operations are subject to complex and changing laws and regulations on subjects including antitrust; privacy, data security and data localization; consumer protection; digital platforms; intellectual property; and environmental, health and safety. The Company is currently subject to antitrust investigations and litigation in various jurisdictions relating to the operation of its app distribution platform, which could result in significant fines and require changes to the Company’s business practices. In fiscal 2024 the Company settled the Orchard Networks patent litigation, and it remains a defendant in other intellectual property matters that could result in additional payments.

Financial Risks

The Company expects its quarterly net sales and results of operations to fluctuate.

The Company’s profit margins vary across its products, services, geographic segments and distribution channels. The Company’s gross margins are subject to volatility and downward pressure due to a variety of factors, including industry-wide product pricing pressures, increased component costs, and the mix of products and services sold.

The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs on the value of its inventory and other assets, in addition to purchase commitment cancellation risk.

The Company records a write-down for product and component inventories that have become obsolete or exceed anticipated demand, or for which cost exceeds net realizable value. The Company also accrues necessary cancellation fee reserves for orders of excess products and components.

General Risks

The price of the Company’s stock is subject to volatility.

The Company’s stock price has experienced substantial price volatility in the past and may continue to do so in the future. The Company’s stock price could decline if the Company fails to meet, or if it revises downward, the guidance regarding net sales growth and gross margin that it provides to investors.

Item 1C.  Cybersecurity

The Company’s Chief Information Security Officer leads a cybersecurity program that is overseen by the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. The program is designed to protect the Company’s information systems and customer data and is informed by recognized industry frameworks.

Item 2.  Properties

The Company’s headquarters is located in Cupertino, California. As of September 28, 2024, the Company owned or leased facilities and land for corporate functions, research and development, data centers, retail and other purposes in the U.S. and various other countries. The Company believes its existing facilities and equipment, which are used by all reportable segments, are in good operating condition and are suitable for the conduct of its business.

Item 3.  Legal Proceedings

Orchard Networks Patent Litigation

On August 12, 2024, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with Orchard Networks LLC resolving all pending patent infringement claims between the parties. The settlement is described in Part II, Item 7 and in Note 10 to the consolidated financial statements.

Other Legal Proceedings

The Company is subject to other legal proceedings and claims that have not been fully resolved and that have arisen in the ordinary course of business. The Company does not believe that the outcome of these matters will have a material adverse effect on its financial position.

Item 4.  Mine Safety Disclosures

ITEM 7.   MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 items and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023. Discussions of fiscal 2022 items and year-over-year comparisons between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2022 are not included, and can be found in Part II, Item 7 of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023.

Overview

Fiscal 2024 was a year of modest top-line growth and continued mix-driven margin expansion. Total net sales increased 2% or $7.6 billion to $391.0 billion, driven by higher net sales of Services and Orchard Phone, partially offset by lower net sales of Orchard Pad and Wearables, Home and Accessories. The weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar had an unfavorable impact on net sales of approximately 1 percentage point. Services net sales grew 13% and represented 25% of total net sales, up from 22% in fiscal 2023.

Fiscal 2024 Highlights

During fiscal 2024 the Company announced new Orchard Phone, Orchard Book and Orchard Pad models and expanded its Services offerings with a new subscription bundle. The Company also completed the sale of its Grove accessories business, consolidated its European distribution operations and settled the Orchard Networks patent litigation, each of which is discussed below under “Items Affecting Comparability.”

Items Affecting Comparability

The Company’s results of operations for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 include the following items that management does not consider indicative of the Company’s ongoing operating performance:

Litigation settlement. During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, the Company recorded a one-time charge of $410 million to settle the Orchard Networks patent litigation. The charge is included in selling, general and administrative expense. The Company does not expect further payments under the settlement agreement.

Restructuring. Restructuring charges of $185 million in fiscal 2024 related to the consolidation of the Company’s European distribution operations, consisting of $128 million of severance and other employee-related costs and $57 million of lease exit and facility costs. The program was substantially complete as of September 28, 2024, and the Company expects annualized cost savings of approximately $220 million beginning in fiscal 2025.

Gain on sale of business. In the first quarter of fiscal 2024 the Company completed the sale of its Grove accessories business for $1.1 billion in cash and recognized a pre-tax gain of $260 million, which is included in other income/(expense), net. Grove contributed net sales of $1.9 billion and operating income of $90 million in fiscal 2023.

Goodwill impairment. Fiscal 2023 included a goodwill impairment charge of $95 million related to the Company’s Home Devices reporting unit, reflecting a reduction in the long-term revenue forecast for smart speakers. No impairment was recorded in fiscal 2024.

Excluding these items, operating income would have been $123.9 billion in fiscal 2024 compared with $114.4 billion in fiscal 2023, an increase of 8%.

Orchard Phone. Orchard Phone net sales were relatively flat in fiscal 2024 compared to fiscal 2023, as higher net sales of the Pro models were offset by lower net sales of the entry models and the unfavorable currency impact.

Orchard Pad. Orchard Pad net sales decreased 6% due primarily to lower net sales of Orchard Pad Pro and the entry-level Orchard Pad, reflecting a difficult comparison against the fiscal 2023 launch.

Services. Services net sales increased 13% due primarily to higher net sales from advertising, cloud services and digital content subscriptions. Paid subscriptions across the Company’s platform exceeded 1 billion at the end of fiscal 2024.

Gross Margin

Products and Services gross margin and gross margin percentage for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 were as follows (dollars in millions):

20242023
Products gross margin$ 109,633$ 108,803
Services gross margin71,05060,345
Total gross margin$ 180,683$ 169,148
Products gross margin percentage37.2%36.5%
Services gross margin percentage73.9%70.8%
Total gross margin percentage46.2%44.1%

Total gross margin percentage increased 210 basis points to 46.2% in fiscal 2024, driven by a higher mix of Services net sales and lower component costs, partially offset by the unfavorable currency impact. Services gross margin percentage increased 310 basis points due to a different Services mix and leverage on fixed costs. The Company expects the Services mix shift to continue to support gross margin expansion, although the rate of expansion is expected to moderate as memory and display component costs rise in fiscal 2025.

Operating Expenses

Research and development expense increased 5% or $1.4 billion to $31.4 billion in fiscal 2024, driven by increases in headcount-related expenses and investments in artificial intelligence features. Selling, general and administrative expense increased 4% or $0.9 billion to $25.9 billion, and included the $410 million litigation settlement charge and $185 million of restructuring charges described above. Excluding those items, selling, general and administrative expense increased 2%.

Other Income/(Expense), Net

Other income/(expense), net was income of $702 million in fiscal 2024 compared with expense of $565 million in fiscal 2023. The change was driven primarily by the $260 million gain on the sale of the Grove accessories business and higher interest income, partially offset by higher interest expense on commercial paper.

Provision for Income Taxes

Provision for income taxes was $19.8 billion in fiscal 2024, and the effective tax rate was 15.9% compared with 14.7% in fiscal 2023. The increase was driven by a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion related to the impact of a European General Court decision on state aid, partially offset by a higher mix of foreign earnings taxed at lower rates. The Company does not expect this state aid charge to recur.

Segment Operating Performance

Americas net sales increased 3% driven by Services and Orchard Phone. Europe net sales increased 7%, driven by Services and Orchard Phone, and included the benefit of the restructuring savings in the second half of the year. Greater China net sales decreased 8% due primarily to lower net sales of Orchard Phone and Orchard Pad and the weakness of the renminbi. Japan net sales increased 3% and Rest of Asia Pacific net sales increased 4%.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

The Company believes its balances of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond. As of September 28, 2024, the Company had $65.2 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and $96.7 billion of total term debt and commercial paper outstanding. Cash generated by operating activities was $118.3 billion in fiscal 2024. The Company returned $110.2 billion to shareholders through share repurchases of $95.0 billion and dividends of $15.2 billion.

Outlook

For fiscal 2025 the Company expects net sales to grow in the low-to-mid single digits, with Services growth in the low double digits and Orchard Phone growth in the low single digits as new artificial intelligence features drive an upgrade cycle. The Company expects gross margin percentage in the range of 46% to 47% and operating margin to expand modestly, reflecting the restructuring savings and continued Services mix shift, partially offset by higher research and development investment. These expectations are forward-looking statements that are subject to the risks described in Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K.

Critical Accounting Estimates

The preparation of financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses. Critical accounting estimates include uncertain tax positions, the useful lives of long-lived assets, and the valuation of goodwill for the Company’s reporting units. The Company performs its annual goodwill impairment test in the fourth quarter of each fiscal year.

Item 7A.  Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

The Company is exposed to economic risk from interest rates and foreign exchange rates. The Company uses various strategies to manage these risks; however, they may still impact the Company’s consolidated financial statements.

Interest Rate Risk. The Company’s exposure to changes in interest rates relates primarily to its investment portfolio and outstanding debt. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in market interest rates would have resulted in a decline in the fair value of the Company’s investment portfolio of approximately $2.8 billion as of September 28, 2024.

Foreign Exchange Rate Risk. The Company’s exposure to foreign exchange rate risk relates primarily to its operations in Europe, Greater China and Japan. A hypothetical 10% adverse movement in foreign exchange rates would have resulted in a decline in the fair value of the Company’s foreign currency derivative instruments of approximately $2.5 billion as of September 28, 2024.

Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements

Note 1 – Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Fixture Fruit Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries. Intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated. The preparation of these consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions.

Note 2 – Revenue

Net sales disaggregated by significant products and services and by reportable segment are disclosed in Note 11. Revenue is recognized when control of the promised products or services is transferred to customers.

Note 3 – Divestiture

On December 15, 2023, the Company completed the sale of its Grove accessories business for cash consideration of $1.1 billion. The Company recognized a pre-tax gain of $260 million on the sale, which is included in other income/(expense), net in the consolidated statement of operations for fiscal 2024.

Note 4 – Restructuring

In the second quarter of fiscal 2024 the Company initiated a plan to consolidate its European distribution operations. Total restructuring charges of $185 million were recognized in selling, general and administrative expense in fiscal 2024. As of September 28, 2024, $31 million of accrued restructuring liabilities remained, all of which are expected to be paid in fiscal 2025.

Note 10 – Commitments, Contingencies and Litigation

During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, the Company recorded a charge of $410 million in connection with the settlement of the Orchard Networks patent litigation, which was paid in full in September 2024. The Company is subject to other legal proceedings and claims that have not been fully resolved.

Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
